title: Service Stability Ambassador Program & Tooling Rundown
content:
Purpose:
This doc describes a cross-functional "Service Stability Ambassador" pilot that pairs product feature teams with a rotating set of SRE ambassadors plus a small suite of lightweight tooling to speed SLO adoption, unblock runway for rollouts, and capture human-in-the-loop learnings. The emphasis: fast experiment cycles (90 days), low ceremony, measurable uplift to SLO observability and incident time-to-detect.

Scope:
- Ambassadors: 2 full-time SREs rotating 6-week stints + 4 part-time liaisons from Serving, Platform, Console, and Product.
- Tooling: Slack probe bot (latency pulse), quick dashboard templates in Console, a CI gatecheck for critical SLO regressions, and a lightweight incident capture template (small JSON form).
- Teams targeted: Hosted API, Dedicated (one pilot pool), and Console rollout teams.

Success metrics (90d):
- 50% of participating feature teams have instrumented at least one SLO in Console (latency or availability).
- Median time-to-detect regressions decreases by 30% for those services.
- Runbook coverage score >= 2 for pilot services (simple checklist present + owner assigned).

High-level approach:
1) Incubation week (wk0): orientation, baseline telemetry capture, quick win backlog.
2) Activation (wk1-4): onboarding sessions, install slack probe, deploy dashboard templates, define SLO(s), small experiment with caching/batching knobs.
3) Stabilization (wk5-9): SLO alerts tuned, CI gate enabled on a subset of PRs, runbook rehearsals, champion handoff to team owners.
4) Retro and scale plan (wk10-13): collect metrics, document playbook, recommend next cohort.

90-day timeline (detailed):
- Day 0-7: Kickoff meeting, identify 3 pilot services, collect current latency P95/P99 and error rates, unblock missing metrics (trace IDs, kv cache hit rate).
- Day 8-21: Deploy Slack probe bot to each service channel (config: 1m synthetic latency check hitting warm path), import dashboard template (latency, error budget burn, request size distribution).
- Day 22-35: Define SLOs collaboratively (examples below), set initial alert thresholds, triage any instrumentation gaps.
- Day 36-60: Runbook dry-runs + tabletop for top two failure modes, enable CI gate for PRs touching serving pipeline, iterate on alert thresholds to reduce noise.
- Day 61-90: Compile results, create one-page handoff playbook per service, present findings to Eng Leaders, decide next cohort.

Suggested SLO examples (to be adapted per service):
- inference-api: Objective: 99.5% successful responses within 200ms P95 over 30d window. Indicator: request latency (server-side) and status code != 5xx.
- model-predict-batch: Objective: 99.9% job completions within SLA window (2h) for scheduled batches. Indicator: job success, queue wait time, retry counts.
Note: keep SLOs focused (1 latency or 1 availability per service) for pilot simplicity.

Onboarding checklist for ambassador -> feature team pairing:
- Pre-kickoff: share current dashboards, PR pipeline access, and owner contacts.
- Day 1: Run a 45m practical session (instrumentation walkthrough + how to import dashboard).
- Week 1: Verify traces contain request_ids and model_name tag; fix missing tags.
- Week 2: Agree on SLO definition, set targets, schedule alert cadence.
- Week 3: Publish a one-paragraph runbook and assign oncall owner.

Tooling rundown (what we will ship for pilot):
- Slack Probe Bot (sre-tools/probe-bot): posts synthetic latency checks, auto-creates a ticket when burn rate spikes. Minimal config: endpoint, warm header, acceptable P95.
- Console Dashboard Templates: small JSON exports for latency, error budget, kv-cache-hit, model-size distribution. Copyable via Console -> Templates.
- CI Gate (sre-ci-check): simple step that runs a synthetic load at PR stage for model-serving changes (10s warm run). Will fail PR if latency regresses beyond threshold set by an SLO tag.
- Incident Capture Form: tiny schema (service, timeline, severity, signal, immediate mitigation, owner) that writes to a shared Google Sheet for the cohort.

Runbook snippet (example):
- Symptom: sustained P99 latency > 1s for inference-api for > 3 minutes.
- Immediate actions: 1) Check Console dashboard for traffic spikes; 2) Run probe-bot manual check; 3) If API error rate > 5% open emergency channel and call SRE ambassador.
- Mitigations: increase batch size (if safe), roll back recent model change, route 10% traffic to fallback variant.

Training & engagement plan:
- Week 0: 60m "SLO basics for product teams" lecture (recorded).
- Week 2: 90m lab: import dashboard, create SLO, link to alerting. Hands-on.
- Week 5: Tabletop incident rehearsal (30m + 30m retro).
- Office hours: weekly 30m drop-in with ambassadors.
- Slack channel: #stability-ambassadors for quick Qs and probe-bot alerts.

Experiment backlog (examples):
- A: Try prefix-KV cache warmup and measure delta in P95 for long prompts.
- B: Short-circuit route for small tokens to a quantized model variant and measure quality/regression.
- C: CI synthetic load for embedding pipelines to detect batch size regressions early.

Dependencies & quick wins:
- Need small Console feature toggles: template import UX and permission to let ambassadors create ephemeral dashboards for teams.
- Require a short GitHub Actions runner (sre-ci-check) permission to run on PRs.
- Quick win: enable probe-bot and set a single threshold for one pilot service; this should reveal immediate instrumentation omissions.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: noise from immature alerts -> Mitigation: start with very conservative thresholds and use a burn-rate style escalation.
- Risk: teams see ambassadors as extra overhead -> Mitigation: ambassadors do the heavy lifting early and ship artifacts the team owns at handoff.
- Risk: tooling permission friction -> Mitigation: pre-book 1:1 with infra/security to get minimal perms and document them.

Open questions / decisions required:
- Should ambassador rotation be paid time or backfill? (ops cost vs hiring).
- CI gate extent: block on all PRs touching serving-runtime or only opt-in per repo?
- Measurement: canonical dashboard for cohort vs per-service dashboards?

Immediate next steps (this week):
- Confirm pilot service list and stakeholders (owners and Slack channels). (Owner: Aisha)
- Create Console dashboard template PR and place in linked_artifacts. (Owner: Liam)
- Standup 30m kickoff with ambassadors + pilot teams (schedule by Nov 6).

Notes to self / rough ideas:
- Consider a small "ambassador badge" (digital) awarded to teams who complete the handoff playbook.
- Keep playbook one pager; long docs won't be read.
- Track time ambassadors spend per team in a simple sheet to inform next cohort sizing.

Appendix: quick contact list
- SRE Ambassadors: Aisha Patel (lead), Liam Chen.
- Platform partner: Marco Rivera.
- Product lead (Hosted API): Priya Kapoor.

End of doc.
